problem: Answers to the same question change depending on extra-linguistic context (when and where the question is asked), yet the standard static QA evaluation paradigm does not measure adaptation to new contexts.
method: Identify context-dependent questions in existing open-retrieval QA datasets via annotation/heuristics, crowdsource alternative contexts and their answers, then evaluate whether existing open-retrieval systems answer with up-to-date facts when given an updated evidence corpus.
key_assumptions: Context-dependence can be identified and crowdsourced for existing questions
Temporal context is adequately represented by a date
Adaptation to new facts is tested by swapping in an updated retrieval corpus
main_contribution: SituatedQA, a dataset of questions with alternative temporal/geographic contexts and answers, plus an empirical demonstration that open-retrieval QA does not adapt to updated facts even with an updated corpus.
datasets: 9K questions annotated from four existing open-retrieval QA datasets (e.g., NQ-Open) with alternative temporal/geographic contexts and answers
baselines: Open-retrieval QA systems (retriever-reader pipelines, e.g., DPR-style) trained on past data with an updated evidence corpus
results: Roughly 16.5% of NQ-Open questions are context-dependent; state-of-the-art retrieval-based systems with an updated corpus are 15 percentage points less accurate on questions asked in the present; models struggle on frequently updated answers.
limitations: Temporal context is a date, with no versioning, supersession or near-duplicate revision structure
The corpus-update test replaces documents rather than tracking amendments to the same text
Covers temporal and geographic contexts as a joint study
future_work: Open-retrieval QA benchmarks should incorporate extra-linguistic context to stay relevant globally and in the future

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: Diagnoses the problem (retrieval QA does not adapt to updated facts) rather than proposing a temporal relevance term; its notion of temporal context is a question date over a web QA corpus, not a validity interval over near-duplicate amended clauses.
relation_to_idea.basis: Full text and abstract confirm time-dependent answers and retrieval failure on updated corpora; however the paper proposes no temporal ranking component and its corpus lacks amendment/version structure.
